The diff does make all nine tests pass, but it introduces a behavior — "a word immediately after a colon is treated like the first word of the text and is never lowercased" — that is **not described anywhere in the docstring**. The docstring's rule 2 only exempts the first and last word of the whole string from lowercasing; by that literal spec, "a" in `"notes from the field: a year of remote work"` should stay lowercase, yet `test_subtitle_after_colon` expects `"A"`.

Since the teammate explicitly said the docstrings are the source of truth, the right fix here is to also update the docstring to state the colon-following-word exception (or, if that's not actually the intended rule, to reconsider the implementation). As written, the `is_after_colon` branch reads like logic reverse-engineered specifically to make `test_subtitle_after_colon` pass rather than something derived from the documented contract — the docstring and the code now disagree about what happens after a colon, which will mislead the next person who reads only the docstring.

Please update the docstring to accurately describe the colon behavior (and any other undocumented cases the implementation relies on) before merging, so docstring and code stay in sync.

Aside from that, the rest of the logic (uppercase-preservation, small-word lowercasing, first/last capitalization, punctuation stripping) looks correct and matches the documented rules.
